_meta.purpose: External SWE-bench Verified baseline claims for models Drake is weighing for local (256GB-class hardware) runs, gathered so his own model-eval gauntlet results have something to sit next to. See README.md in this directory for the full caveat on why these numbers are directional-only against model-eval's own task results.
_meta.collected_by: research seats (per Drake handoff, seat: implementer, studio/baseline-data)
known_gaps: source_urls is empty on every record: the handoff that produced this file listed numbers and named evaluators but no URLs. Needs a follow-up pass from the research seats that gathered the numbers before this file can be cited externally.

fits_256gb and quant_planned are null except where Drake's handoff stated one explicitly (Kimi K2.5). The rest are unassessed, not confirmed-fitting -- absence of a flag here is not evidence the model fits.
contamination_flag is null except where an explicit audit was cited (DeepSeek V4-Flash). Null means unassessed, not clean.

models.notes: No independent SWE-bench Verified reproduction found as of the handoff date. Vendor-only figure -- treat as an upper bound.
Independent (Scale AI) and vendor figures match within 0.2pp -- the cleanest corroboration in this set.

Naming ambiguity in the handoff: the benchmark values were recorded against 'DeepSeek V4' while the model list names 'DeepSeek V4-Flash'. Recorded here under the list name -- verify these are the same model before citing. Vendor claim (80.6) sits 6.6pp above the NIST CAISI figure (74.0) before contamination is even accounted for. A held-out audit flagged an additional 8% pass@1 leakage rate on top of that gap -- this is the least trustworthy vendor number in the set.

Vendor figure is 'best of 3 scaffolds', not a single fixed harness -- already an optimistic-selection number before any independent check exists. Treat as an upper bound, not a like-for-like comparison point.

Vendor and independent (Fireworks) figures are identical. Explicitly flagged by Drake as NOT fitting a 256GB host -- out of scope for the local-model runs this baseline is meant to support unless that changes.

Largest vendor/independent gap in this set: 21.8pp (72.2 vendor vs 50.4 vals.ai). No contamination audit cited either way -- the gap alone is reason to weight the vals.ai figure over the vendor figure until more is known.

No vendor SWE-bench Verified claim was in the handoff for this model -- only a community reproduction of approximately 62 (stated as '~62', not a precise score). independent_source does not match one of the four named evaluators (Scale AI / NIST CAISI / Fireworks / vals.ai) -- lowest-confidence entry in this file, treat as a rough anchor only.
